messages:
jin: Anyone seeing weird retry auth behavior after rotating creds locally?
tara: what sort of behavior?
jin: Node SDK will pick up new REDWOOD_API_KEY immediately for new requests, but when a request fails and the SDK retries, the retry attempt sometimes uses the old token. leads to 401 loops.
oscar: that sounds like token captured at request start and reused for retries. we probably do getToken() once and stash it.
jin: exact repro: start a long polling call, rotate creds via local-agent (it writes ~/.redwood/creds.json and exports REDWOOD_API_KEY), trigger a mid-request transient 401 (simulate by expiring token). original request -> 401 -> retry. retry uses stale auth header. log snippet: "[req=abc] auth=old_tok -> 401; retry auth=old_tok -> 401"
tara: thanks. we intended retries to re-check credentials on 401 to handle rotation. parity note: python client always re-fetches token on retry; js client does not.
mohit: that's a parity bug then. recommend: policy = re-fetch token on 401 retry only (not on all retries) to avoid extra calls for KMS-backed providers.
oscar: agreed. implement small change: on retry after authentication failure (401/403) call CredProvider.refresh() and then resend with new header. keep previous behavior for non-auth failures.
jin: also: we need to be careful with project/org env changes. if REDWOOD_PROJECT_ID changes mid-run we should not silently switch routing. that should raise an error and force restart.
tara: yup. add invariant: project/org are init-only; env change => logger.warn + throw on next request.
mohit: config knobs: expose client option credHotReload: boolean (default true) and env REDWOOD_CRED_HOTRELOAD=false to opt-out. document in SDK readmes.
oscar: small API suggestion: expose Client.refreshCredentials(force=false) so apps can explicitly refresh after rotation hooks. avoids surprises for infra with strict semantics.
ci-bot: PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/998 - fix: retry re-fetch token on auth failure; add credHotReload flag (CI: tests pass) :rocket:
jin: awesome, thanks. can we also add a sample app script that exercises rotate+retry? e.g., examples/rotate-and-retry.sh that runs a loop, rotates creds, then hits endpoint to validate behavior.
tara: will add sample and a small integration test that asserts no 401 loops when rotation occurs.
mohit: one more edge: atomic rename rotation on linux/osx can mean file inode changes; for file-backed provider use mtime+sha1 checksum check to detect change. mention in docs.
oscar: good catch. logging: emit info when token source switches (env -> file or file -> kms) and when a retry triggers credential refresh. makes debugging easier for devs.
jin: noted. created GH issue #1509 to track parity across SDKs (js/py/go) and link to the PR. tagging @eng-sdk.
tara: thanks all. i'll follow up with the sample app PR and update readme sections on env conventions and restart semantics. :pray:
